https://technode.com/2026/07/22/catl-to-.text: Credit: CATL CATL has signed a 2 GWh agreement with Solarpro, a leading renewable energy company in Central and Eastern Europe, to deploy its Tener Sodium energy storage system. The two companies plan to jointly develop the first large-scale sodium-ion battery energy storage project in the region later this year. The project will use CATL’s Tener Sodium energy storage system, which offers a cycle life of up to 15,000 cycles and is designed to operate reliably for 25 to 30 years. The system also delivers strong low-temperature performance, retaining 92% of its capacity at -20°C, making it well suited to the harsh winter conditions in Eastern European countries such as Lithuania, where temperatures can fall to -15°C to -20°C. CATL and Solarpro have maintained a long-term strategic partnership since their first collaboration in 2024, when they deployed a 150 MWh EnerC+ liquid-cooled battery energy storage system in Bulgaria. In May this year, the companies connected a 602 MWh Tener lithium battery energy storage system to Bulgaria’s power grid, increasing the country’s total energy storage capacity by approximately 10%. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/18/megj.text: Menü Kereső Megjelent a teljes, 482 oldalas dokumentum arról, hogyan manipulálták az Orbán-kormányok idején a híreket az MTI-nél Belföld frissítve Klág Dávid Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom A Duna Médiaszolgáltató Zrt. kedd délután közzétette a teljes, 482 oldalas dokumentumot, ami azokat az eseteket gyűjti, amikor a Magyar Távirati Irodában (MTI) manipulálták a híreket. A dokumentumról augusztus elején lehetett először hallani, amikor az MTI újságírói átadták az MTVA új vezetésének, amely alapján a Duna Médiaszolgáltató Zrt. vezetése belső vizsgálatot rendelt el. A magukat Pro Domo munkacsoportnak nevező tudósítók és hírszerkesztők több mint 10 éven át gyűjtötték a levelezéseket, emaileket, csetüzeneteket, amik bizonyítják, hogyan manipulálták, hamisították, hallgatták el az ország egyik legfontosabb hírforrásának számító MTI-nél a híreket. A munkacsoport úgy fogalmazott, hogy ezek az esetek „nyilvánvalóan ellentétesek a szerkesztőségi alkalmazottak munkaköri leírásával, az MTI Szerkesztőségi Kézikönyvével, a 2010. évi CLXXXV. törvénnyel, illetve a jogszabály alapján készített Közszolgálati Kódexszel és az Alaptörvénnyel”. A munkacsoport több kategóriára osztotta az eseteket: elhallgatott vagy parancsra készített hírek; kidobott hírek; manipulált anyagok; cenzúrázott és hamis hírek. A dokumentum szerint a Pro Domo tagjai a gyűjteményt Narancs csíkosnak nevezték el, ami az úgynevezett „piros csíkos bizalmasként” emlegetett kiadványra utal, ami azokat a jelentéseket tartalmazta, amiket a nyugati hírügynökségek készítettek, de a hazai közvélemény előtt nem jelentek meg. Az MTVA augusztus elején egy 15 oldalas válogatást is közölt a dokumentumból , amely állításuk szerint a rendelkezésre álló iratanyag reprezentatív válogatását képezi. A TELJES PDF-ET EZEN A LINKEN LEHET LETÖLTENI. A végleges, 482 oldalas irat ugyanazt a struktúrát követi, mint a tizenöt oldalas kivonat: tematika szerint rendszerezve, időrendben, belső levelezésekből kiragadott részletekkel sorolnak az MTI rendszerében megjelent, vagy éppen nem megjelent híreket. Bizonyos MTI-szerkesztők neve olvasható a szövegben, de sok dolgozó nevét kihúzták. Vannak olyan levelek, amiket a rossz felbontás miatt nem lehet elolvasni. A dokumentumban külpolitikai hírek és témák szerepelnek, belpolitikai hírek nem, ezért a magyar politikai szereplők nevei nincsenek a szövegben, Szijjártó Péter kivételével. Olyan anyag nem jelenhetett meg, amiben nemzetközi szervezetek bírálták Orbán Viktort, vagy amiben téma volt a magyar sajtószabadság helyzete. Pár példa a dokumentumból: „A kijevi tudósító váltig állítja, hogy Olaf Scholz német kancellár Kijevben azt mondta, hogy nem tudjuk mit tegyünk. Ilyen az eredeti leirat szerint a sajtótájékoztatón nem hangzott el”. „[A szerkesztő] napok óta minden nap anyagot készíttet arról – többnyire hiteltelen és semmilyen komolyan vehető hírügynökség által nem idézett, jobboldali amerikai lapokból-, hogy Hillary Clinton egykori elnökjelölt kampánycsapata John Durham különleges ügyész beadványa szerint kémkedett Donald Trump után.” „A magyar állami hírügynökség nem számolt be róla (címes-leades főhírben), hogy a két állam közötti diplomáciai kapcsolatfelvétel 30. évfordulóján, egy potenciális orosz-ukrán fegyveres konfliktus árnyékában, Volodimir Zelenszkij ukrán elnök és Orbán Viktor magyar kormányfő először beszélt egymással. A telefonos kapcsolatfelvétel során Zelenszkij kijevi látogatásra hívta meg Orbánt. A tény maga megjelent az MTI-ben az […] ismét Ukrajnát ostorozó Szijjártó-közlemény legalján eldugva.” „Szergej Lavrov orosz külügyminiszter április 10-én éjjel az általa vezetett tárca honlapján megjelentetett egy nyilatkozatot a Szijjártó Péterrel folytatott, lehallgatott és kiszivárogtatott telefonbeszélgetéseinek egyikéről. Az állami média irányítói, többórás ”érlelés„ után a dobás mellett döntöttek, feltehetően azért, mert nem ítélték hasznosnak a választási kampány szempontjából.” […] át kell írni egy hírügynökségi hírt az ukrajnai háborúról úgy, hogy egy idézett szereplő kijelentéseivel kezdődjön, ne hírügynökségi összefoglaló a legfrissebb eseményekről legyen a lead, mert a cenzorok nem szeretik a hírügynökségek értelmezéseit, magyarázatait. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c804.text: Image source, Getty Images By Benedict Garman Â and Â Matt Murphy ,Â BBC Verify Published 5 hours ago Russia fired its new rapid, jet-powered drones against Ukraine every day throughout August, BBC Verify analysis of Ukrainian Air Force data has found, escalating its use of a weapon that Kyiv's air defences are struggling to deal with. It marked the first time that daily attacks by Moscow's new upgraded Geran drones were recorded in Ukrainian Air Force data. The growing use of jet-propelled and other varieties of drones prompted President Volodymyr Zelensky to condemn what he called an unfolding "horror" over the skies of Kyiv. Ukraine's military recently told the BBC that jet-powered drone attacks grew from 350 in June to 1,600 in July and 2,800 in August. In five of the nightly attacks in August, these drones outnumbered the older, slower models. "The reason for turning to jet-powered drones is that they are much faster than the previous generation and it makes it much more difficult for Ukraine to intercept them," said Dr Marina Miron, an expert on military technology at King's College London. The upgraded munitions can cruise at more than 300mph, significantly faster than older models and well beyond the top speed of Kyiv's interceptors. The drones are powered by turbojet engines, some of which, according to Ukrainian military intelligence, are sourced from China. According to Zelensky, the drones were used as part of a wave of attacks that killed at least 12 people and injured 20 more on 1 September. Six of the casualties were railway workers after a depot was hit in Kyiv. And on Wednesday the Moldovan government said a plane carrying Zelensky was delayed at Chisinau airport on Tuesday after a Russian drone - reported to be jet-powered - entered Moldovan airspace. Earlier this year Ukraine showed relative success in countering Russian drones and was intercepting 94% of long-range drones, according to Zelensky . But the speed of the newer drones has prompted the latest round in Kyiv and Moscow's arms race. On 10 August, Ukraine's deputy head of military intelligence, Maj Gen Vadym Skibitskyi, said his forces needed new interceptor missiles "capable of matching [jet-drones'] speed". Image source, Reuters Image caption, Debris from Geran drones' distinctive jet engines has become increasingly common in Kyiv Four Ukrainian companies have reportedly started testing missiles that can shoot down the new Geran models, officials in Kyiv recently told reporters. The country's new defence minister, Yevhenii Khmara, has tasked them with producing "thousands of units" as quickly as possible. Russia also had an economic incentive to invest in the jet-powered drones. The increased speed and manoeuvrability of these models means the line between them and more expensive cruise missiles has become "blurred", said John Hardie of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, a think tank focused on national security and foreign policy. "Long-range one-way attack drones are basically a poor man's cruise missile," he said. "The more you add capability to a drone, the less meaningful the distinction between the drone and a lower-end cruise missile." But the analyst organisation Conflict Armament Research emphasised that jet-drones are not yet as advanced as cruise missiles. It said the munitions have a shorter attack range, carry much smaller warheads and are more susceptible to jamming systems. Meanwhile, satellite images appear to show Moscow is redesigning key facilities dedicated to fighting the war in Ukraine to host jet-powered drones, with longer rails associated with the munitions visible at an entirely new base at Tsymbulova in the Oryol region. Multiple launch sites appear to have been built at the facility, which is around 109 miles (175 km) from the Ukrainian border. Since the facility became operational, Tsymbulova appears to have become a key centre for Russian drone attacks. Oryol region, where the Tsymbulova base is located, was not mentioned as a drone launch site in Air Force reports before September 2024, but by August 2026 it was named in almost every attack. The proliferation of jet-powered drones comes as BBC Verify found that Russia is now striking Ukraine with complex attacks involving hundreds of drones and missiles about once a week. The increase in the size of the strikes is being powered by Moscow's shift towards combining a "greater variety of munitions" - including jet-powered and decoy drones - with expensive ballistic missiles that are extremely difficult to intercept, analyst Michael Bohnert of the RAND think tank told BBC Verify. Kyiv's data shows that Moscow is now using over 15 times more drones per attack than it was four years ago. Bohnert added that the tactically complicated nature of the assaults, coupled with a global shortage of air defence systems capable of halting ballistic missiles partly caused by the US-Israeli war with Iran, has led to falling interception rates by Ukraine. Ukraine's Air Force data showed a drop in interceptions of ballistic missiles up to the end of July. In August, Kyiv mostly stopped publishing the figures that would show its interception rate. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Rail industry Railway engineering work over Christmas will cause 10 days of disruption London Paddington and Birmingham New Street stations will shut for five days but most routes will stay open Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent Sat 31 Oct 2026 07.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Passengers travelling on some of Great Britain’s busiest railway lines at Christmas have been warned of significant disruption from 10 days of engineering works. Work will close London’s Paddington station – affecting intercity trains to the west of England and Wales until January – as well as Birmingham New Street, the UK’s busiest station outside the capital, for five days over the holiday period. Passengers travelling between London , north-east England and Scotland will have to negotiate the part closure of the east coast mainline on Christmas Eve. Direct trains from the capital to parts of Essex and Norfolk will also be cut for much of the festive period. Network Rail said most routes would still stay open and that the Christmas period, when train services generally stop for 25 and 26 December, remained the best time to conduct essential works. Engineers hope to use the quieter festive days to carry out about £152m of works to improve reliability and capacity. The biggest engineering work is expected on the lines leading into London Paddington, including replacing a junction near Slough. Most Great Western services to Wales and the west of England will start and finish at Reading, with some services diverting around Oxford to London Euston, from 27 December until 4 January. Stratford International on track to get cross-Channel trains in budget boost Read more The work also means Elizabeth line services west of Paddington and Heathrow Express services will not resume after Christmas until 31 January. Birmingham’s main station, New Street, will be closed from the start of Christmas Eve until 29 December to replace overhead power supplies. No trains will stop or pass through, with rail replacement buses serving the city centre. Passengers using east coast mainline services run by LNER and other operators may wish to avoid travel on Christmas Eve. Work at Doncaster means trains between London, north-east England and Scotland will be partly replaced by rail replacement buses from Newark to York, adding two hours to journeys. The Great Eastern mainline out of London Liverpool Street will be closed for 10 days from Christmas Day for track replacement in east London, meaning no Greater Anglia or Elizabeth line rains will run through the area, with no direct trains from Norwich to London. TransPennine services between Leeds and Manchester will be slowed for six weeks from Christmas Day with the closure of Huddersfield station. Network Rail’s group director, system operator, Anit Chandarana, said: “Christmas is a time when many people want to be with family and friends, and most of the railway will be open to help them get there. We have worked with train operators to keep services running wherever we can on the busiest travel days and to provide alternative journey options where work affects the usual route. “We are sorry that some passengers will face disruption. The days between Christmas and new year are by far the quietest of the year and give us the best opportunity to complete major projects such as the power supply upgrades at Birmingham and Paddington. Our teams will do everything they can to keep people moving, and we urge passengers to check their journeys before setting off.” Explore more on these topics Rail industry Network Rail Rail transport Transport London Birmingham Wales news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland
